title: Service Providers: Who Does What
summary: The roles of the main service providers to a fund, including the depositary, investment manager, prime broker, distributor, auditor and legal adviser, and how they work together.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The roles of the main service providers to a fund, including the depositary, investment manager, prime broker, distributor, auditor and legal adviser, and how they work together.
Learning Objectives: Describe the role and duties of each main service provider
Explain the depositary's safekeeping, cash monitoring and oversight duties
Recognise how service providers interact across a fund's operations
Syllabus: The depositary: safekeeping, cash flow monitoring and oversight
The investment manager and the prime broker
Auditors, legal advisers and other specialist providers
Intended Audience: New joiners and graduates at fund managers, administrators, depositaries and other fund service providers
Operations, client service, finance, technology and support staff who need a grounding in funds
Staff moving into the funds industry from banking, insurance or other sectors
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of investment funds is required. The programme is suitable for new joiners, graduates and staff moving into the funds industry.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
IOSCO, Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes (2018)
IOSCO, Recommendations on Sustainability-Related Practices, Policies, Procedures and Disclosure in Asset Management (2021)
